name: Flag social drafts that look like your last 30 posts (wording + structure)

parameters.content:
## What this does

Before you publish, it compares each **ready** draft against your **last 30 published posts** and flags the ones that will read as "more of the same".

Most duplicate checks compare **words**. That misses the real problem: you can write 30 posts that share no vocabulary and still feel identical, because every one of them opens with "You…", ends with "comment below", and runs the same 14-line / 5-paragraph rhythm. Readers get bored by the **shape**, not the nouns.

So this checks both:

- **Wording** — bigram overlap (Jaccard) against each past post
- **Structure** — four signals: opening pattern, ending type, line/paragraph rhythm, filler-phrase set

A draft is only flagged when **both** are true: wording overlap is above the threshold **and** at least two structural signals match. Either one alone is normal and does not flag.

The flag writes back **which past post it clashes with and which signals matched**, so you know what to change — not just a score.

## Setup

1. Two Google Sheets tabs — `Drafts` (columns: `id`, `text`, `status`, `note`) and `Published` (columns: `text`, `published_at`).
2. Connect your Google Sheets credential on the three Sheets nodes and pick your document.
3. Connect Slack on the last node, or replace it with Telegram / Discord / Gmail.
4. Put `ready` in a draft's `status` column and activate. Runs daily at 09:00.

This never publishes anything. It only writes `needs rework` or `approved` back into your sheet — your publishing workflow decides what to do with that.

## Tune it here

Inside **Compare drafts to history** there are three numbers at the top:

- `WORD_OVERLAP` — how much bigram overlap counts as "similar wording". Default `0.18`.
- `STRUCTURE_HITS` — how many of the four structural signals must match. Default `2`.
- `HISTORY` — how many past posts to compare against. Default `30`.

**Both** conditions must trip before a draft is flagged. Raising either number makes the gate quieter.

If you write in a language without spaces (Chinese, Japanese, Thai), the bigram comparison already works on characters — nothing to change.

## Why it writes a reason, not a score

"87% similar" tells you nothing you can act on.

This writes back the offending post plus the exact signals, e.g.

`needs rework — reads like "How I stopped…" (2026-08-03): same opening ("You…"), same ending type (comment-bait), 22% wording overlap`

That sentence tells you which knob to turn: change the opening, or change the ending, or change the angle.
